messages:
Maya Lee: heads up, noticed console tiles (sparklines + heatmap) are stalling intermittently after the rollout that disabled aggressive prefetching.
Adrian Chen: saw a spike in FCP/LCP metrics? https://grafana.redwood/d/console/perf-overview?snapshot=abc123
Maya Lee: yeah LCP up ~700ms on heavy dashboards, repro locally w/ 30s load test.
Samir Patel: repro steps?
Maya Lee: open dashboard with 12 panels, switch time range, scroll. Tiles blank for ~1500ms then render. CPU not fully saturated but main-thread shows long task.
Kevin Ortiz: could be bundle split causing parse+eval hang when prefetch is off. dynamic imports firing at scroll time.
Maya Lee: copying a snippet from performance profiler: 
```
LongTask (duration 1123ms)
  parseScript: 542ms
  instantiateModule: 220ms
  evaluate: 430ms
  stack: fetch->compile->execute
```
Adrian Chen: is KV cache miss correlated to the stall?
Maya Lee: yes — after the rollout kvcache miss rate jumped from ~5% -> ~48% for dashboard assets.
perfbot: Alert: metric console.kv_cache.miss_rate exceeded threshold (5m avg = 48%).
Samir Patel: that aligns with the prefetch-disable change. previously we primed kv with chunk bundles ahead of scroll.
Kevin Ortiz: routing/quota angle: the prefetched route used a high-priority token bucket; the change removed that bypass so prefetch was essentially throttled.
Maya Lee: proposal A: restore prefetch for top N dashboards (by traffic) + add telemetry tag for chunk_load_latency and kvcache_hit.
Adrian Chen: proposal B: change prefetch to low-priority background with higher concurrency but strict rate limit, so it doesn't consume quota for interactive requests.
Samir Patel: also propose adding sample-based stack traces at render pause to capture the hot parse frames. lightweight (1% sampling).
Kevin Ortiz: short-term quickfix: rollback prefetch flag for EU canary and roll forward the memoized dom ref PR later.
deploy-bot: @kevin Ortiz initiated canary rollback for prefetched-assets flag in EU at 2025-09-14T16:02:00Z :rotating_light:.
Adrian Chen: I'll add a Grafana panel: chunk_download_time and kvcache_miss_rate, split by route and user_tier. also add alert if mean chunk_load_ms > 200ms.
Maya Lee: thanks — i'll run a canary load test post-rollback and post results here.
Samir Patel: FYI, found a small perf win: memoize computed DOM refs during hydration to shave ~120ms on heavy panels. PR #4124 in review.
Maya Lee: great. if rollback looks good we'll keep prefetch but tune policy + land memoize. will update after load test.
Adrian Chen: putting a short action list: 1) rollback canary (kevin) 2) create telemetry panels + alerts (adrian) 3) run canary load (maya) 4) land memoize PR and sample profiler (samir).
Maya Lee: sounds good — keeping this thread as the landing place for results. :thumbsup:
